context: Ridgeline (ridge) plot showing KDE score distributions for 10 evaluation criteria, comparing before vs. after calibration states, with 120 synthetic data points per criterion and a toggle button to hide/show the 'after' distributions.
first_impression: Clean and immediately readable — the two-color overlap tells the before/after story at a glance without any decoding effort.
what_works: The two-color palette (rose vs. blue) is perceptually distinct and alpha-blended well so overlap zones are legible rather than muddied; dashed median markers anchor precise location without adding visual clutter. The 65% row overlap compresses 10 distributions into a single scannable column where the rightward shift and narrowing of 'after' curves reads as a global pattern instantly.
what_doesnt: The legend label 'After calibration' is visually truncated in the rendered output due to tight right-margin positioning, breaking the legend's legibility. The wide 'before' tails on low-scoring criteria (Accessibility, Responsiveness) bleed into adjacent rows, making individual row baselines ambiguous — a slightly taller row height or reduced overlap would help. Animation quality of the entrance and toggle transitions cannot be assessed from the static screenshot.
